title: Head-box bounds on the last coordinate
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $lo,hi:\mathrm{Fin}(k)\to\mathbb{Z}$, let $clo,chi\in\mathbb{Z}$, and let $p:\mathrm{Fin}(k+1)\to\mathbb{Z}$. Suppose the last coordinate of $p$ lies in $[clo,chi]$, and each of its first $k$ coordinates lies in the corresponding interval $[lo_j,hi_j]$. Then every coordinate of $p$ lies in the corresponding interval whose bounds are formed by adjoining $clo$ and $chi$ as the last-coordinate bounds.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ at the last coordinate lies in $[clo,chi]$
